title: Sets Quiz
description: Check your knowledge of Python sets, uniqueness, and union and intersection.

questions.prompt: What is the main property of elements in a Python set?
options: Each value appears at most once
They are stored in insertion order only
questions.explanation: Sets store unique elements; duplicates are ignored automatically.

questions.prompt: Which literal creates a set with two items?
questions.explanation: Curly braces with comma-separated values define a set (not an empty dict).

questions.prompt: How do you create an empty set?
questions.explanation: {} creates an empty dictionary; use set() for an empty set.

questions.prompt: A set can contain the same value twice if you add it twice.
questions.explanation: Adding a duplicate has no effect; the set still holds one copy.

questions.prompt: What does s.add(3) do when 3 is not already in set s?
questions.explanation: add() inserts a single element if it is not already present.

questions.prompt: Which method removes a specific element from a set?
questions.explanation: remove(x) discards x and raises KeyError if x is missing.

questions.prompt: What is the result of len({1, 1, 2, 2})?
questions.explanation: Duplicates collapse, so the set is {1, 2} with length 2.

questions.prompt: Which operator returns elements in either set A or B?
questions.explanation: | is union: all elements that appear in A or B (or both).

questions.prompt: The expression {1, 2} & {2, 3} evaluates to {2}.
questions.explanation: & is intersection: only elements in both sets, here {2}.

questions.prompt: What does A & B return?
options: Elements in both A and B
Elements in A but not B
Elements in exactly one of A or B
questions.explanation: Intersection keeps values that appear in every operand set.

questions.prompt: What is list({3, 1, 2}) most likely to show?
options: A list of three unique numbers; order is not guaranteed
An error because sets cannot convert to lists
questions.explanation: Sets are unordered; converting to a list gives arbitrary order.

questions.prompt: How do you test membership in a set s?
questions.explanation: Use the in operator: x in s is True when x is in the set.

questions.prompt: What does s.discard(x) do if x is not in s?
questions.explanation: discard() removes x if present and silently does nothing otherwise.

questions.prompt: You can use a list as an element inside a set.
questions.explanation: Set elements must be hashable; lists are mutable and unhashable.

questions.prompt: Which builds a set from a list with duplicates removed?
questions.explanation: Passing a list to set() returns a set of unique values.

questions.prompt: What does A - B mean for sets?
options: Elements in both A and B
Elements in A but not in B
Elements in B but not in A
Symmetric difference of A and B
questions.explanation: Difference A - B is elements that are in A and not in B.

questions.prompt: What is {x for x in 'hello' if x != 'l'}?
questions.explanation: Curly braces with a for clause define a set comprehension.

questions.prompt: After s = {1, 2}; s.update([2, 3]), what is s?
questions.explanation: update() adds multiple elements; duplicates are ignored.

questions.prompt: Sets are mutable: you can add and remove items after creation.
questions.explanation: Regular sets support add, remove, and other mutating methods.

questions.prompt: Why might you use a set to filter duplicates from a list?
options: Sets preserve the original list order exactly
Sets automatically keep only unique values
Sets are faster only for empty lists
questions.explanation: Converting to a set drops duplicates; you may convert back to a list if needed.
